tagline: The world's second-largest atoll is one giant protected lagoon — a natural home for silent electric flight.
summary: Rangiroa is the flagship of the Tuamotu atolls: a lagoon roughly 80 km long — the second-largest atoll on earth — ringed by a coral rim with two famous passes, Avatoru and Tiputa, where resident dolphins draw divers from around the world. Every guest experience here happens by boat inside the lagoon: the pass corridor, the ~20 nm run to the Blue Lagoon, dive sites, pearl farms and motu picnics. It is a captive, repeatable day-loop market on flat protected water, currently served entirely by outboard skiffs — the cleanest possible fit for quiet, emission-free foiling in a fragile coral ecosystem.

use_cases.title: The Blue Lagoon day-loop, transformed
use_cases.body: The ~20 nm Avatoru → Blue Lagoon run is the atoll's signature excursion, today a 1-hour-plus pounding ride in an open skiff that cancels when the lagoon kicks up. A foiling shuttle flies above the wind chop in ~45 smooth minutes, runs silent past the bird islets, and makes the loop reliable in trade-wind season.

use_cases.title: Pass-corridor dive and dolphin shuttle
use_cases.body: Dive boats shuttle the short Avatoru↔Tiputa corridor all day, timed to the tidal currents. An electric foiling tender does it with no engine noise over the dolphins' home pass and no fuel sheen on a living reef.

use_cases.title: Resort-to-motu private charter
use_cases.body: Kia Ora and the pensions sell motu picnics, pearl-farm visits and sunset runs — all inside-lagoon hops under 25 nm. A silent foiling charter is the premium version of every one of them, with zero emissions in a closed lagoon ecosystem.

use_cases.title: Tuamotu inter-atoll links
use_cases.body: Tikehau — the neighbouring postcard atoll — lies ~35 nm west, and Papeete sits ~190 nm away. Quanta-LR connects the atoll chain and the capital without any charging infrastructure on the outer islands, complementing the all-electric fleet inside the lagoon.

journeys.today: ~20 nm across the open lagoon in an outboard skiff: over an hour each way, wet and jarring when the maramu trades blow, and trips cancel outright in strong wind.
journeys.with_navier: A ~45-minute flight above the chop — dry, silent, no spray, no fuel smell — turning the atoll's marquee excursion into part of the experience itself.

journeys.today: Constant small-boat shuttling along the 2–10 nm north-rim corridor between the two passes, villages and resorts — outboards idling over the reef and the resident dolphin pod.
journeys.with_navier: A near-silent electric foiling tender working the pass corridor all day on one charge — no noise over the dolphins, no wake against the motu shorelines.

journeys.today: No scheduled boat link — visitors backtrack via Air Tahiti through the air network or charter an open-ocean crossing.
journeys.with_navier: A ~35 nm direct hop between the two most-visited Tuamotu atolls, opening two-atoll itineraries that today require a flight connection.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire visitor economy lives inside one protected lagoon: Avatoru↔Tiputa pass corridor (2–12 nm), Blue Lagoon (~20 nm), Reef Island, L'Aquarium and pearl-farm hops — all flat-water, all far inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, with multiple rotations per charge. Solar-plus-storage at the resort pier covers charging on an atoll grid.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR carries the network beyond the rim: Tikehau ~35 nm west in all weather, Fakarava and the dive-circuit atolls further down the chain, and Papeete ~190 nm southwest — all without depending on charging infrastructure that the outer Tuamotus don't have.

competitive_landscape: On-water service today is fragmented small operators: dive centres (Topdive, The Six Passengers, Rangiroa Diving Center) running outboard RIBs to the passes, family excursion boats doing the Blue Lagoon loop, resort tenders, and the inter-island cargo schooners (Papeete cobra/supply ships calling roughly weekly with goods). There is no scheduled inter-atoll passenger boat and no premium on-water tier at all — every tourist rides the same open skiffs. The volume, repetition and fixed routes of the excursion market are the demand evidence; the absence of any modern vessel is the opening.

precedents.what: ~$100M, ~100-vessel electric foiling network with JIH Global, first 5 vessels in 2026
precedents.why_it_matters: The closest analogue on earth: dispersed atoll resorts, protected lagoons, no grid on outer islands — proof the playbook works at national scale in exactly this geography.

seasonality: Tropical and operable year-round. The drier April–October season brings the steady maramu southeast trades that chop up the long lagoon fetch — the main cause of wet rides and cancelled Blue Lagoon trips, and exactly the conditions foiling flies over. November–March is warmer and wetter with occasional north swells working into the passes; the passes themselves run strong tidal currents, so operations time around slack and ebb like the dive boats already do.
regulatory_note: French Polynesia operates under French maritime law (Affaires Maritimes) with territorial oversight from the Direction Polynésienne des Affaires Maritimes — an established, navigable certification path for commercial passenger craft. The territory's tourism strategy leans heavily on lagoon protection and 'slow, clean' positioning, and the Tuamotus' coral ecosystems make a zero-emission, no-wake, silent fleet a direct policy fit; UNESCO-listed Fakarava biosphere reserve next door sets the conservation tone for the whole archipelago.
